## Overview

AeoLiS models are usually described by a configuration file, `aeolis.txt`, with one
`key = value` line per parameter and input data in separate text files. Aeolis.jl reads
these files, runs them as `aeolis run` does, and writes netCDF output in the AeoLiS layout.
This vignette runs one of the AeoLiS regression cases, a transect with tides, waves, runup,
vegetation and avalanching, and compares the result with aeolis-python
[@deVries2023].

```{julia}
#| output: false
ENV["GKSwstype"] = "100"
using Aeolis
using NCDatasets
using Plots
```

## Reading a configuration file

The case ships with the package tests. Its configuration file names the grid, bed, wind,
tide and wave files, which `read_config` loads relative to the file's directory. Keys that
AeoLiS itself ignores (this file has six, such as `process_nelayer`) are skipped with a
warning, which is hidden here.

```{julia}
case = joinpath(pkgdir(Aeolis), "test", "data", "case1_small_waves")
readdir(case)
```

```{julia}
#| warning: false
p = read_config(joinpath(case, "aeolis.txt"))
```

Spatial files hold one row per grid row, as in AeoLiS; they are stored with x as the first
dimension. Time series keep their columns:

```{julia}
size(p.xgrid_file), size(p.wind_file), p.wind_file[1:3, :]
```

## Running it

`run_config` solves the problem with the scheme and solver of the file and, because
NCDatasets is loaded, writes the output file:

```{julia}
#| warning: false
out = joinpath(mktempdir(), "aeolis.nc")
sol = run_config(joinpath(case, "aeolis.txt"); outputfile=out)
```

The netCDF file has the AeoLiS dimensions `s`, `n`, `time`, `layers` and `fractions`, with a
transect written as a single row:

```{julia}
NCDataset(out) do ds
    [(k, size(ds[k])) for k in keys(ds) if k in ("x", "zb", "mass", "Ct", "time")]
end
```

```{julia}
zb = transect(sol, :zb)
plot(sol.u.x[:, 2], zb[:, 1]; lw=2, label="initial", xlabel="x (m)", ylabel="bed level (m)")
plot!(sol.u.x[:, 2], zb[:, end]; lw=2, label="after $(sol.t[end] / 3600) h")
```

## Agreement with aeolis-python

The test data also hold `reference.nc`: the full model state of aeolis-python after every
time step of the same case, in double precision. Stepping the Julia model alongside it
compares every step:

```{julia}
ref = NCDataset(joinpath(case, "reference.nc"))
pyzb = Array(ref["zb"])           # (x, y, step): netCDF's (step, y, x) reversed
integ = init(AeolisProblem(p); save_vars=Symbol[])
diffs = Float64[]
for k in 1:(size(pyzb, 3) - 1)
    step!(integ)
    push!(diffs, maximum(abs.(integ[:zb] .- pyzb[:, :, k + 1])))
end
close(ref)
diffs
```

The largest difference in bed level over these steps is at the level of round-off:

```{julia}
maximum(diffs)
```

## Writing configuration files

`write_config` writes parameters back to a configuration file, with input arrays in text
files next to it, so a model built in Julia can be run by aeolis-python:

```{julia}
dir = mktempdir()
write_config(joinpath(dir, "aeolis.txt"), p)
filter(f -> endswith(f, ".txt"), readdir(dir))
```

```{julia}
q = read_config(joinpath(dir, "aeolis.txt"))
q.xgrid_file ≈ p.xgrid_file && q.wind_file ≈ p.wind_file && q.grain_size == p.grain_size
```
